subject: Microsoft's agents get work accounts, like employees
preview: Google's Gemini 4 Neon nears the top models for less, Anthropic prices its IPO, Slack agents take standing orders, and Google previews an agent that tends apps after launch.

News from Wednesday, November 18, 2026 · Read on the web

What matters today

Image: Microsoft

Microsoft Ignite, the recap

Microsoft wraps two days of agent launches at Ignite 2026.

  • Agents as staff: Autopilot, Teams agents and Foundry agents get their own Entra identity, some a mailbox and a place in the org chart.
  • Copilot first: Office and Code move into the Copilot app, and Microsoft IQ offers the same company context to outside agents.
  • For builders: the Copilot SDK 2.0 and a Foundry harness open Microsoft's own agent engine; Agent 365 adds controls and costs.

Why it matters
Microsoft now treats an agent like a new hire: a name in the directory, a mailbox, a seat in Teams and an admin who can switch it off. Agent products will be judged on how they fit that seat.

See all 46 Ignite announcements, with pictures and videos ↓

Image: Google

Gemini 4 Neon

Google releases Gemini 4 Neon for long agent tasks.

  • Price: $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, with a 1 million-token context; rolling out in the Gemini API and to Pro and Ultra subscribers.
  • Google's figures: third overall at 61 on the Artificial Analysis index, at 32% lower cost per task than Gemini 4 Carbon on its default setting.

Why it matters
A model one step below the top now scores close to it for less per task. For most agent products the cheaper tier becomes the default, and the top model is saved for the hardest steps.

Anthropic goes public

Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share.

  • The offering: 980,000,000 Class A shares, most sold by Anthropic; trading starts November 19 on Nasdaq under ANT.
  • More to come: underwriters may buy up to 147,000,000 more shares within 30 days; the offering is set to close November 20.

Why it matters
Claude's maker will now report revenue, costs and risks every quarter. Builders who depend on Claude get a regular public read on its business that private labs never give.

Slack agents take recurring jobs

Slack gives agents a Tasks tab for recurring work.

  • How it works: in an agent's direct message, people hand it standing jobs, like a morning digest or a weekly report, and it runs them on its own.
  • On by default: developers can switch it off; it needs Slack's newer agent view and the assistant:write permission.

Why it matters
Slack teaches people to give an agent standing orders, not just questions. Agents for work chat now need a schedule and a record of runs, not only a reply.

Image: Google

Agents that maintain apps

Google Labs previews Stitch Loop, an agent for after launch.

  • What it does: connects to a codebase and live product data, finds security, speed and accessibility problems, and opens pull requests for a person to approve.
  • Stage: an experiment with a waitlist; it connects through over 180 integrations and custom MCP servers.

Why it matters
Coding agents so far stop when the code ships. Stitch Loop takes on the work that follows, keeping a live product healthy, and moves the agent from builder to owner.

Research worth watching

Agents that remember why they changed

A log of each harness change, its reason and its result helps an agent keep improving when the model or test changes: 2.36 points higher on average in coding.

Why it matters
Keep a change log for your agent setup; it pays off at every model swap.

A test for agents that make slides and sites

211 tasks across slides, graphics, video and web pages. Nine setups scored 42 to 71, and most of the gap came from quality, not from meeting the brief.

Why it matters
Agents meet the brief; what separates them is whether the result is good.

How much 4-bit models really change

On two decision models, server and engine changes moved under 1% of answers, while 4-bit versions changed 3.5% to 5.8%.

Why it matters
Test a smaller model on your own decisions; accuracy scores hide the flips.

An assistant that speaks first

AURA 2.0 watches live video, starts a conversation when something is worth saying, and calls tools based on what it sees.

Why it matters
Proactive assistants need rules for when to speak up uninvited.

What developers are debating

A Berlin guide site loses most of its readers: its founder says Google AI Overviews took most of his traffic after seven years of growth; 781 points and 695 comments.

AI answers and clicks: a randomized test that hid Google AI Overviews from some US users found they cut clicks to outside sites by about 40%; 697 points, 547 comments.

Audit agents against auditors: KPMG UK says more than 100 AI agents sometimes asked better questions than its audit team; 457 points, 211 comments.

Top launches yesterday

S.Space
One shared workspace where a team and AI agents from different vendors hand off tasks and share memory.
Bluedot Phone Calls
Takes notes on phone calls, and on meetings, without a bot joining.
Toone
A Mac app where agents run recurring jobs you describe in plain words.
Waldo by Wherobots
An agent that writes and runs map and location analyses from plain-English requests.
Dippr
Agents build and run a company's internal tools on its own data, with access rules.
Pitch Avatar HR Suite
Talking AI avatars for onboarding, training and staff updates.

Ignite 2026: all 46 announcements

Both days of Ignite, each announcement linked to its own page, with pictures and videos where Microsoft published them, grouped by what it changes for someone building a product with AI.

The launches that matter most

01
Autopilot Frontier
A personal agent with its own identity, memory and tools that keeps working on a task without new prompts.
Key detail: Rolling out to Frontier customers from November 17; an Entra Agent ID for Autopilot agents is in preview.

Why it matters
The assistant stops waiting to be asked. Work products now need to say what an agent may do while nobody is watching.

02
Teams agents as colleagues Preview
Agents receive Entra accounts, join chats, channels and meetings, can be @mentioned and can post without being asked, within set limits.
Key detail: Foundry hosted agents can also get an email address, a Teams presence and a place in the org chart.

Why it matters
Teams becomes the place agents are hired into. An agent that cannot sit in a chat or a meeting will look like a tool, not a teammate.

03
Microsoft Copilot SDK 2.0 Generally available
Lets developers build the agent engine Microsoft and GitHub run in production into their own apps, with many users served from one runtime.
Key detail: Rebuilt in Rust, one test turn went from 5.25 seconds to 55.3 milliseconds; six programming languages; announced November 17.

Why it matters
Writing your own agent loop becomes optional. The edge moves to what the agent knows and is allowed to do, not the loop that runs it.

04
Microsoft IQ Generally available
One place for a company's data, skills and tools, which Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Foundry and other agents reach over MCP.
Key detail: It brings Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ together, with no new license to buy.

Why it matters
Company context becomes something Microsoft sells to every agent, including ones it did not build. Whoever holds that context shapes how good each agent's answers are.

05
Copilot Code and Managed Runtime Frontier
Describe a dashboard, tracker or app in plain words and Copilot builds it, then runs it inside the company's own tenant.
Key detail: Copilot Code reaches general availability in December; Copilot Managed Runtime, which hosts and governs these apps, is generally available now.

Why it matters
Any employee can now make the small internal app they used to request. Makers of simple internal tools now compete with a button inside Copilot.

06
Agent 365 for local agents Preview
Coding agents on a PC, starting with GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code, get an Entra Agent ID that IT can see and control.
Key detail: Admins can also choose who may use each plugin and skill in Copilot and Cowork, now generally available.

Why it matters
Agents on laptops stop being invisible to IT. A coding agent sold to companies will need to show up in that list and follow its rules.

Everything else, by what it changes

Copilot becomes where work starts

  • Home in the Copilot app Rolling out
    One starting point for Chat and Cowork; Auto suggests moving a complex task to Cowork and carries the context across.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • Office in Copilot and Today Generally available
    Word, Excel and PowerPoint run in the Copilot app, saving to OneDrive.
    Key detail: Today, which turns mail, meetings and chats into priorities and drafts to approve, is in private preview.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • Copilot Workspaces Frontier
    A shared space where a team and Copilot track changes, questions and actions; it replaces Copilot Notebooks.
    Key detail: Workspace memory is in public preview; personal Autopilot agents are coming to Workspaces.
  • Copilot Credits Coming in December
    People who reach their license limits keep using a chosen model, paid by usage.
    Key detail: Cloud PCs for agents from Windows 365 for Agents can be paid with the same credits.
  • Copilot on Windows Preview
    Copilot finds, moves and renames files on the PC, explains PC problems, and opens from the new Windows Search.

Why it matters
The chat app, not Office, is now the front door, and heavy use is billed by the meter. Products that live inside Microsoft 365 must show up in Copilot to be found.

Agents join the team

  • Agent Accounts Coming in December
    Copilot Studio agents that stay on and take delegated work through documents, email or Teams.
    Key detail: Public preview is scheduled for December.
  • Foundry hosted agents Generally available
    Agents built with a company's own code run on Microsoft's service, with network limits and crash recovery.
    Key detail: Running them on your own clusters is targeted for early December.
  • Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Public preview
    Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox; a team brings the knowledge, skills and tools.
    Key detail: Voice agents that people can interrupt mid-sentence are generally available in Foundry.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • Computer use and browser automation in Foundry Generally available
    Agents use apps through the screen and isolated cloud browsers, with a live view and a button for a person to take control.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • Windows 365 for Agents Available
    Agents get managed Cloud PCs for apps with no API, as a tool in Copilot Studio.
    Key detail: Foundry access comes in preview early next year; always-on Cloud PCs for agents are in Frontier preview.
  • Edge for Business Preview
    IT can make agents browse in Edge, each in its own window with its own identity.
    Key detail: A skills recorder turns a task done in Edge into a reusable Cowork skill.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • Azure SRE Agent and deployment agent Public preview
    The operations agent now works in Teams and with other agents.
    Key detail: The deployment agent, which turns plain requests into infrastructure code, is generally available. November 17.
  • Azure Catalyst Generally available
    One place to plan and run moves of apps, databases and servers to Azure, with an agent that does the migration work.
    Key detail: Announced November 17; the agent's new modernization features are in preview.
  • SQL and PostgreSQL database agents Preview
    Agents watch databases, explain problems and suggest or run approved fixes.
    Key detail: Database Hub in Fabric, one view of databases across clouds, is generally available.

Why it matters
Agents now get what an employee gets: an account, a computer, a browser and a seat in the chat. The hard part moves from building one agent to managing a staff of them.

Company data, for any agent

  • Work IQ Generally available
    Agents search and remember across Microsoft 365 with each person's permissions, and take on longer tasks.
    Key detail: Reacting to new messages without a prompt, and finer approval controls, are in preview.
  • Foundry IQ and Fabric IQ Preview
    Foundry IQ maps how documents connect so agents cite sources; Fabric IQ answers from a company's agreed numbers.
    Key detail: Fabric IQ connectors for ChatGPT and Claude are in preview.
  • Web IQ Generally available
    Web pages, news, images, places and weather for agents and apps, open to all Azure customers at a lower price.
    Key detail: Product data for shopping agents, 40 billion+ listings, is in private preview.
  • Salesforce in Copilot Public preview
    Sellers get Salesforce data and permitted actions inside Copilot, with 38+ sales skills.
    Key detail: Sales Cloud in Teams is in a pilot; Salesforce and Fabric share data without copying it.
  • Dynamics 365 in Copilot Generally available
    Sales, customer service and finance plugins bring Dynamics 365 work into Copilot and Excel.
    Key detail: Agents to scope moves off SAP ECC are rolling out.
  • Fabric apps and Rayfin Generally available
    Ready backends (database, sign-in, services) for business apps on company data, including apps made in Copilot.
    Key detail: More than 100,000 apps built since preview.
  • Azure HorizonDB and other databases Generally available
    A managed PostgreSQL database with built-in vector search; Cosmos DB adds a semantic reranker and a Rust SDK.
    Key detail: Redis 8 with an agent kit is in preview.

Why it matters
Company context is now for sale to every agent, Microsoft's and others'. Agents will be judged on the data they can reach, and data products will be built to be read by agents.

Models and tools for builders

  • MAI models and Decision-1.1 Generally available
    Seven Microsoft models for coding, images, voice, transcription and security.
    Key detail: Microsoft's figures: MAI Code 2 gets 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's coding quality at about 40% of the price.
  • Copilot Fusion and browser use Available
    GitHub Copilot mixes several models on one task, and can drive a browser to debug web apps.
    Key detail: Browser use and Copilot Evals, which tests skills and MCP tools, are in public preview.
  • VS Code moves to the Copilot harness Available
    VS Code's agents now run on the same engine as Copilot CLI; the old one goes in February 2027.
    Key detail: In one rollout comparison it used 14.2% fewer tokens per device.
  • Foundry Dev Pack and Toolboxes Generally available
    Foundry's tools for editor, terminal and coding agents in one install; Toolboxes share tools across agents.
    Key detail: An A2A tool links Foundry agents to outside agents.
  • Continuous improvement in Foundry Generally available
    Foundry groups repeated agent failures, scores whole conversations and tests fixes before release.
    Key detail: Expert notes on agent runs and training on your own data are in preview.
  • Frontier Tuning Private preview
    Company experts tune AI skills to their own standards, with a GitHub Copilot plugin, a CLI and publishing to Cowork.
    Key detail: The private preview opens to more customers.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • GitHub Copilot connectors Public preview
    Eight more services, including Supabase, Box and Calendly, connect to Copilot through GitHub-verified MCP servers.
    Key detail: Shared team plugins are generally available.

Why it matters
Microsoft ships its own low-cost models and the engine that runs them. Picking a model turns into reading a price list, and the engine becomes a shared part nobody needs to rebuild.

Keeping agents in check

  • Agent controls Public preview
    One Azure service where companies set rules for what any agent may do, checked before a tool runs or data leaves.
    Key detail: Built on two open-source specs, Agent Hooks and the Agent Control Specification.
  • Agent 365 cost and analytics Frontier
    One view of AI spending with limits and alerts, and a dashboard of what agents cost and deliver.
    Key detail: Cost management is in preview, as is Dynamic Agent Risk, a live risk level for each agent.
  • Microsoft Entra for agents Preview
    Agent IDs extend to Autopilot agents, and network controls now cover local agents and MCP servers.
    Key detail: Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise, which lets agents query Entra data, is generally available.
  • Microsoft Perception and MDASH Generally available
    Security agents test attacks, investigate alerts and rank weak spots; MDASH uses 100+ agents to find real flaws in code.
    Key detail: MDASH is in preview.
  • Defender for local AI agents Generally available
    Checks what coding agents on Windows are told to do for hidden malicious instructions.
    Key detail: Shielding unpatched systems during an attack is in preview.
  • Purview for Copilot and agents Preview
    Stops Copilot from using sensitive files even when they carry no label, and limits what data agents on Windows can share.
  • Agents in Windows containers Preview
    Windows runs each agent in a container with limits on the files and networks it can reach.
    Key detail: A learning mode that watches agents before rules are enforced is generally available.
    ▶ Watch the video
  • AI Transparency Initiative Announced
    Microsoft and more than 40 organizations start shared standards so what models and agents do can be checked independently.

Why it matters
Agents face the checks staff face: identity, permissions, audits and a risk score. Selling agents to companies means passing those checks, and governance becomes something buyers compare.

The infrastructure underneath

  • Agents on your own AKS clusters Preview
    Run Foundry models and agents on your own Kubernetes clusters, with sandboxes for the code agents write.
    Key detail: Confidential computing across several GPUs is in preview.
  • Azure Cobalt 200 Generally available
    Arm-based virtual machines that speed up the work agents do outside the model.
    Key detail: Up to 50% better CPU performance than Cobalt 100.
  • Microsoft and Intel Announced
    A long-term deal: Microsoft's own chips will use Intel's packaging, and Intel Xeon memory and security features come to Azure.
  • Windows and Windows 365 for IT Preview
    Windows Server 2028 is in preview, Cloud PCs can run local AI models, and Intune can block devices running unapproved agents.

Why it matters
Microsoft is building agents into its chips, servers and Windows. Companies that want agents on their own hardware or clusters now get Microsoft's tools there too.

Also in the news

  • Genie 4: Google DeepMind's world model lets Ultra subscribers change a generated world mid-session by typing, now with sound; rolling out.
  • Workday and Honeydew: Workday plans to buy Honeydew, which gives agents and reports the same business definitions so answers match.
  • Vercel Board: an experimental shared board where many agents claim tasks and post progress; v0 built on it merges over 50% of its pull requests.
  • Google Chat agents: developers can add a description and up to three starter prompts to Chat apps and agents, without code.
  • Gemini Notebook: typing "make me a site" turns a notebook's sources into an interactive site.
  • Amazon OpenSearch Memory: lasting memory for agents across sessions, generally available in five regions.
  • Cloudflare Clairic: an updated document extraction model and a 9-billion-parameter Clairic-flash, both with open weights on Hugging Face.
  • DeepSeek: search and web fetches made inside model calls are no longer billed separately; only model tokens count.
  • ElevenAgents for Healthcare: voice agents for clinics with medical transcription, health record links and HIPAA-eligible setups.
  • Inside the Codex sandbox: OpenAI explains how Codex runs commands on your machine within the file and network limits you set.
  • OpenAI and chip design: OpenAI says its models optimized circuits in its Jalapeño chip and improved RISC-V core designs.
  • OpenAI on risk: how it handles frontier risk from training to deployment, and how coding agents speed up its research, unevenly.
  • Le Figaro and OpenAI: summaries and excerpts of Le Figaro journalism come to ChatGPT, with links to the stories.
  • The Silent Consensus: an OpenAI essay on how people can keep control of their institutions as AI grows more capable.
